title: Movement in the rule
hookLine: a daily walk or stretch: Cook Ding's knife followed the natural lines, and his lord learned from it how to nourish life
tomorrow: why does the Torah say to bless God after the meal, not before?

lines: A RIP, A SLICE, A RHYTHM.
HAND, SHOULDER, FOOT, KNEE, IN TIME.
WHAT I LOVE IS THE WAY.
cards: The sound comes first: a soft rip, a slice, a steady rhythm. In the kitchen of a lord named Wen Hui, a cook named Ding is cutting up an ox.
Every move of his hand, his shoulder, his foot, his knee falls in time, like a dance to old court music. The lord stands watching and can hardly believe it. Ah, he says, how can skill go this far?
The cook lays down his knife. What I love, he says, is the Way, and it goes beyond skill.

teach.b: This story is from the Zhuangzi, a classic book of Taoism. Ding explains. When he started, all he could see was the whole ox.
After three years, he no longer saw it whole. Now he meets it with his spirit, not his eyes, and follows the natural lines: the blade slides through the gaps at the joints and never strikes bone.

teach.h: THE GOOD COOK CUTS; THE ORDINARY ONE HACKS.
teach.b: A good cook, he says, changes his knife every year, because he cuts. An ordinary cook changes it every month, because he hacks. Ding's knife has lasted nineteen years and is as sharp as the day it left the whetstone.
And when he comes to a hard knot, he slows down, watches closely, moves his hand gently, and it comes apart.

teach.h: I HAVE LEARNED TO NOURISH LIFE.
teach.b: Then the lord says the line the chapter is named for: from my cook's words, I have learned how to nourish life. Here's the teaching.
In Taoism, nourishing life means caring for the body by following its grain, not forcing it.

Later Taoists, tradition says, used the same words for gentle daily practices of movement and breath. That's the measure for movement in your rule. Not a punishment you hack through until something gives.
A daily walk or stretch that follows the lines your body actually has, slows down at the hard knots, and keeps you sharp for years.

how: Taoist teachers speak of nourishing life, yangsheng, and keep gentle daily movement and breath under that name. On a personal rule, movement can be a daily walk or stretch at a set time.

games.q: what does “movement in the rule” mean?
o: a strict workout plan meant to punish the body into shape
a dance class taken once a year at a special holiday
a daily walk or stretch, written in, following your body's grain

games.q: Cook Ding's knife: tap the pairs.
p: cut up an ox like a dance
the lord who watched and learned
hacks, and changes his knife monthly
slow down, move the hand gently

s: Cook Ding said his secret was years of hard, forceful cutting
he said he follows the natural lines; it's the ordinary cook who hacks.
the lord said his cook had taught him how to nourish life
the chapter of the Zhuangzi is named for it: nourishing life.
Ding's skill meant he never had to slow down
at a hard knot he slows, watches closely and moves gently.

games.q: a friend's new plan: a brutal workout every day "until it stops hurting." what would Cook Ding's way change?
o: follow the body's lines and slow at the knots: move daily without hacking.
nothing: Ding's skill came from forcing his knife through the bone.
skip movement until the body feels perfect, then start.
games.why: Ding's knife lasted because it followed the natural lines, and at hard places he slowed down. The ordinary cook hacks, and wears out his knife.

practice: Stand up, if you can, and stretch slowly: arms overhead, then a gentle twist, then a reach toward the floor. Go only as far as the body opens easily, like Ding's knife finding the gaps.
Where something is tight, slow down and breathe there, and keep moving gently through the sit.

wordCard.voice: Movement in the rule: a daily walk or stretch written into your rule, following your body's grain, the way Cook Ding's knife followed the natural lines.

orig.note: Chinese: nourishing life, the lord's lesson from Cook Ding and the name of the chapter.

carryVoice: Your line: move daily. Cook Ding's knife followed the lines and stayed sharp for years. Day 1646, on your feet.
